components.description: Selective CoT value and visual bottleneck -> shallow visual reflection -> attention bias

nodes.name: CoT is not a free lunch
nodes.description: Multimodal CoT should be applied selectively: it is generally effective on reasoning tasks but can introduce side effects on perception tasks such as visual grounding, knowledge VQA and object counting.

nodes.name: CoT gains on math, science, multi-image
nodes.description: CoT improves performance by 6.1%, 2.9% and 4.9% on mathematical, scientific and multi-image reasoning respectively, consistently across almost all models.

nodes.name: Logical and algorithmic CoT gains depend on scale
nodes.description: For logical and algorithmic reasoning, which rely more on visual information, larger models benefit from CoT while smaller models often show limited or negative gains.

nodes.name: Open-source reasoning models gain little
nodes.description: Existing open-source multimodal reasoning models show only limited gains over their base models across diverse tasks, possibly because RLVR training concentrates on math at the expense of broader reasoning.

nodes.name: Commercial reasoning model gains
nodes.description: Gemini-2.0-Flash-Thinking shows substantial and consistent gains across reasoning tasks, with a 24.7% improvement in algorithmic reasoning.

nodes.name: Visual reasoning errors dominate
nodes.description: A large proportion of CoT errors come from visual reasoning failures, with over 80% in logical reasoning tasks due to incorrect reasoning over visual information.

nodes.name: Visual probes are harder than textual probes
nodes.description: On probes (math probes 93.0% and logical probes 88.5% verified accurate), models score about 20% lower on visual than textual reasoning probes.

nodes.name: Visual probe accuracy correlates more with task performance
nodes.description: Original task performance correlates more strongly (higher Pearson r) with visual probe accuracy than textual probe accuracy, so visual reasoning is the key bottleneck of current MLLMs.

nodes.name: Visual vs verbal reflection
nodes.description: Reflection in multimodal CoT splits into visual reflection (reconsidering the visual input) and verbal reflection (reconsidering its own reasoning).

nodes.name: Look Light, Think Heavy pattern
nodes.description: Verbal reflection rises and peaks mid-way through the CoT, while visual reflection steadily declines over time.

nodes.name: Models fail to abstain when visual info is missing
nodes.description: Despite visual reflection, models show limited ability to abstain from answering when critical visual information is missing, indicating shallow visual reflection.

nodes.name: Attention bias toward reasoning tokens
nodes.description: During long CoT, models (e.g. Kimi-VL-A3B-Thinking) allocate disproportionate attention to reasoning tokens while progressively neglecting visual tokens, which may constrain visual reflection.

isolated_nodes.name: Task taxonomy and scale
isolated_nodes.description: The study covers 12 multimodal tasks split into perception (comprehensive evaluation, OCR, visual grounding, hallucination, knowledge, counting) and reasoning (math, science, logic, algorithmic, spatial, multi-image), tested on 14 non-reasoning and 8 reasoning models.

isolated_nodes.name: Multi-image CoT mechanism
isolated_nodes.description: For multi-image reasoning, MLLMs describe each image in CoT and then reason over the aggregated textual descriptions.

isolated_nodes.name: Future directions
isolated_nodes.description: Models need visual introspection capability and mechanisms to leverage external tools such as the think-with-image paradigm to address visual bottlenecks.

structural_reasoning: Task-level CoT effects and model comparisons are descriptive; the visual-bottleneck chain leads to reflection and attention-bias findings. (Edge P12->P11 is a mechanistic explanation; P10->P12 introduces the attention analysis.)
